original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Determine the shortest unsigned word for the depth-five dirty chain connector z_l += B_l z_{l-1} (l = 1..5, z_0 = x immutable, z_1..z_4 and y = z_5 dirty) over characteristic m, answering open question 2 of PR #4263 in a bounded range: exact minima at m = 2, 3, 4 by exhaustive search, and the per-call floor 5m attained for every nonzero residue c when 9 <= m <= 20.
scope_change_reason: The card asks about one extension of the connector alphabet. This package keeps the unsigned complete-call alphabet and lengthens the one-source chain by one more call, continuing the depth-three and depth-four side questions of PRs #4249 and #4263. It does not extend a source-count census or claim a supplier improvement.
bottleneck_link: A recursive boundary that routes through four dirty intermediates pays this call count. The premium over the floor is larger and lasts longer than at depth four (8m at m = 2, 3; 6m or 7m at m = 4 depending on c) and is gone for 9 <= m <= 20. Side result: no consumer, paid profile or kappa change is supplied.
stop_rule: Stop after exhaustive minima for the smallest characteristics and explicit floor witnesses for every (m, c) in a bounded range, with literal dirty replay and source-bound publication checks. No all-m construction is attempted.
evidence: verify.py runs BFS over all of UT6(Z/m) for m = 2, 3 (and over UT5 for m = 2..5 as a control against #4249), checks 173 floor witnesses (every c for 9 <= m <= 20, eleven pairs at m = 5..8) and three m = 4 words by interval counts, an independent UT6 product and literal dirty replays, and prints a receipt with package and input SHA-256 values. The m = 4 lower bounds come from a full BFS over 4^15 elements, run with verify.py --exhaustive-m4 (about 9 minutes and 20 GB locally; not a registered check).
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What are the exact depth-five minima at m = 5, 6, 7, 8 for the residues with no floor witness here?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would locate exactly where the depth-five premium ends; the search found the 5m floor only for some c in this range.
open_questions.first_step: For each missing (m, c), test whether 6m is attained by annealing with one doubled call (search_witnesses.c accepts count vectors), and exclude 5m by a meet-in-the-middle search over balanced prefixes and suffixes.
open_questions.blocked_by: A full BFS needs m^15 states (3e10 at m = 5); annealing failure at 5m is not a proof of impossibility.

open_questions.question: Is the depth-five minimum exactly 5m for every m >= 9?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would make the premium a small-characteristic effect at depth five as well.
open_questions.first_step: Look for a parametric family of the four interleaving sequences (the depth-five form of #4263 Lemma 2).
open_questions.blocked_by: The depth-four all-m question of #4263 is itself open.

open_questions.question: Why does the m = 4 minimum depend on c (24 for c = 2, 28 for c = 1, 3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A residue-dependent premium suggests a 2-adic obstruction that might be provable by hand and extend to m = 8 or other even m.
open_questions.first_step: Compare the reachable top-corner residues of balanced and one-doubled words at m = 4 and m = 8.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the m = 4 BFS is available; m = 8 is far beyond exhaustive search.
